column2:
oasis(n.)綠洲、宜人之處(複數 oases)
(無詞性變化)
desert oasis 沙漠綠洲
an oasis of calm 寧靜的世外桃源
The exhausted travelers finally reached an oasis in the desert.
(筋疲力盡的旅人終於抵達了沙漠中的一片綠洲。)
The small park is an oasis of calm in the busy city.
(這座小公園是繁忙都市中的一片寧靜綠洲。)

oath(n.)誓言、宣誓、咒罵
(無詞性變化)
take an oath 宣誓
under oath 在宣誓下(作證)
The new president took an oath to protect the constitution.
(新任總統宣誓維護憲法。)
Witnesses must tell the truth under oath in court.
(證人在法庭上宣誓後必須說實話。)

oatmeal(n.)燕麥片、燕麥粥
oat(n.)燕麥(常用複數 oats)
a bowl of oatmeal 一碗燕麥粥
instant oatmeal 即食燕麥片
A bowl of oatmeal with fruit makes a healthy breakfast.
(一碗加了水果的燕麥粥是健康的早餐。)
Oatmeal is rich in fiber and keeps you full for hours.
(燕麥富含纖維，能讓你飽足好幾個小時。)

oblige(v.)強迫、迫使、施恩於
obligation(n.)義務、責任
obligatory(adj.)義務的、強制的
be obliged to 不得不⋯
I'm much obliged. 非常感激。
Drivers are obliged by law to wear seat belts.
(依法規定，駕駛人必須繫安全帶。)
I felt obliged to help him after all he had done for me.
(在他為我做了那麼多之後，我覺得有義務幫他。)

obsess(v.)使著迷、使困擾
obsession(n.)著迷、執念
obsessive(adj.)著迷的、強迫性的
be obsessed with 對⋯著迷
obsessed fan 狂熱粉絲
He is obsessed with getting perfect scores on every test.
(他執著於每次考試都要拿滿分。)
Many teenagers are obsessed with checking social media.
(許多青少年熱衷於查看社群媒體。)

obstinate(adj.)固執的、頑固的、難以去除的
obstinacy(n.)固執
obstinate refusal 斷然拒絕
obstinate stain 頑強的汙漬
The obstinate old man refused to listen to his doctor's advice.
(那位固執的老人拒絕聽從醫生的建議。)
It took hours to remove the obstinate stain from the carpet.
(花了好幾個小時才把地毯上頑強的汙漬清除。)

occurrence(n.)發生、事件
occur(v.)發生
common occurrence 常見的事
rare occurrence 罕見的事
Traffic jams are a common occurrence in big cities.
(塞車在大城市是常見的事。)
Snow in Taipei is a very rare occurrence.
(台北下雪是非常罕見的事。)

octopus(n.)章魚
(無詞性變化)
grilled octopus 烤章魚
octopus balls 章魚燒
An octopus can change its color to hide from enemies.
(章魚能改變顏色以躲避敵人。)
We ordered grilled octopus at the seafood restaurant.
(我們在海鮮餐廳點了烤章魚。)

odor(n.)氣味、臭味
odorless(adj.)無味的
body odor 體臭
unpleasant odor 難聞的氣味
An unpleasant odor came from the trash can in the kitchen.
(廚房的垃圾桶傳來一股難聞的氣味。)
Carbon monoxide is dangerous because it has no odor.
(一氧化碳很危險，因為它沒有氣味。)

offshore(adj.)近海的、離岸的、境外的
(無詞性變化)
offshore wind farm 離岸風場
offshore island 離島
Taiwan is building many offshore wind farms to produce clean energy.
(台灣正在興建許多離岸風場來生產乾淨能源。)
Kinmen and Matsu are offshore islands of Taiwan.
(金門和馬祖是台灣的離島。)

offspring(n.)後代、子女(單複數同形)
(無詞性變化)
produce offspring 繁衍後代
healthy offspring 健康的後代
Parents naturally want the best for their offspring.
(父母自然希望給子女最好的。)
Sea turtles leave their offspring alone soon after laying eggs.
(海龜產卵後不久便讓後代自生自滅。)

operative(adj.)運作中的、有效的
operate(v.)運作、動手術
operation(n.)運作、手術
become operative 開始生效
the operative word 關鍵字眼
The new train line will become operative next year.
(新的鐵路線將於明年開始營運。)
The rule is still operative, so we must follow it.
(這項規定仍然有效，所以我們必須遵守。)

oppress(v.)壓迫、使沉重
oppression(n.)壓迫
oppressive(adj.)壓迫的、悶熱的
oppressed people 受壓迫的人民
feel oppressed 感到壓抑
The cruel ruler oppressed the poor for decades.
(那位殘暴的統治者壓迫窮人長達數十年。)
She felt oppressed by the heavy pressure of exams.
(她被沉重的考試壓力壓得喘不過氣。)

oppression(n.)壓迫、壓制、沉悶
oppress(v.)壓迫
oppressive(adj.)壓迫的
political oppression 政治壓迫
fight against oppression 反抗壓迫
The people finally rose up against years of oppression.
(人民終於起身反抗多年來的壓迫。)
Many writers have described life under political oppression.
(許多作家描寫過在政治壓迫下的生活。)

ordeal(n.)嚴酷的考驗、痛苦的經歷
(無詞性變化)
go through an ordeal 經歷苦難
terrible ordeal 可怕的折磨
The hikers were exhausted after their ordeal in the mountains.
(那些登山客在山中歷經磨難後筋疲力盡。)
Preparing for the college entrance exam can be a real ordeal.
(準備大學入學考試可能是一場真正的考驗。)

orderly(adj./n.)有秩序的、整齊的、(醫院)勤務員
order(n./v.)秩序、命令
orderliness(n.)整齊
in an orderly manner 有秩序地
orderly room 整齊的房間
The students left the building in an orderly manner during the fire drill.
(消防演習時學生們有秩序地離開大樓。)
The hospital orderly helped move the patient to another room.
(醫院勤務員協助把病人移到另一間病房。)

organizer(n.)組織者、主辦人、收納盒
organize(v.)組織、籌辦
organization(n.)組織
event organizer 活動主辦人
desk organizer 桌上收納盒
The organizers expect over ten thousand people at the festival.
(主辦單位預計將有超過一萬人參加這個節慶。)
As the event organizer, she handled every detail carefully.
(身為活動主辦人，她仔細處理每個細節。)

orient(n./v.)東方、使適應、使朝向
orientation(n.)方向、新生訓練
oriental(adj.)東方的
orient oneself 確定方位、適應
be oriented toward 以⋯為導向
It took me a few days to orient myself in the new city.
(我花了幾天才熟悉這座新城市。)
The program is oriented toward helping beginners.
(這個課程以幫助初學者為導向。)

oriental(adj./n.)東方的、東方人
orient(n.)東方
oriental culture 東方文化
oriental art 東方藝術
The museum has a large collection of oriental art.
(這間博物館收藏了大量東方藝術品。)
Many Western tourists are interested in oriental culture.
(許多西方遊客對東方文化很感興趣。)

originate(v.)起源、發源、創始
origin(n.)起源
original(adj.)原始的、原創的
originate from 起源於
originate in 發源於
Bubble tea originated in Taiwan in the 1980s.
(珍珠奶茶於1980年代起源於台灣。)
The idea originated from a conversation between two students.
(這個想法起源於兩名學生之間的一次對話。)

ornament(n./v.)裝飾品、裝飾
ornamental(adj.)裝飾用的
Christmas ornament 聖誕裝飾品
ornamental plant 觀賞植物
We hung colorful ornaments on the Christmas tree.
(我們在聖誕樹上掛了五彩繽紛的裝飾品。)
The old temple is ornamented with beautiful carvings.
(那座古廟飾有精美的雕刻。)

orphanage(n.)孤兒院
orphan(n.)孤兒
grow up in an orphanage 在孤兒院長大
volunteer at an orphanage 在孤兒院當志工
He grew up in an orphanage and later became a successful doctor.
(他在孤兒院長大，後來成為一位成功的醫生。)
Our class volunteered at a local orphanage last winter.
(我們班去年冬天到當地的孤兒院當志工。)

orthodox(adj.)正統的、傳統的、東正教的
orthodoxy(n.)正統觀念
orthodox method 傳統方法
Orthodox Church 東正教會
The teacher used an unusual rather than an orthodox method.
(那位老師使用的是一種特殊而非傳統的方法。)
His ideas challenged the orthodox views of the time.
(他的想法挑戰了當時的正統觀點。)

ounce(n.)盎司(重量單位)、少量
(無詞性變化)
an ounce of gold 一盎司黃金
not an ounce of 一點也沒有
The price of an ounce of gold has risen sharply this year.
(今年一盎司黃金的價格大幅上漲。)
He doesn't have an ounce of patience with lazy people.
(他對懶惰的人一點耐心也沒有。)

outbreak(n.)(疾病、戰爭等的)爆發
break out(v.)爆發
outbreak of war 戰爭爆發
disease outbreak 疾病爆發
The outbreak of the flu forced the school to close for a week.
(流感爆發迫使學校停課一週。)
Many families fled the country after the outbreak of war.
(戰爭爆發後許多家庭逃離了這個國家。)

outgoing(adj.)外向的、友善的、即將離職的
(無詞性變化)
outgoing personality 外向的個性
outgoing president 即將卸任的總統
With her outgoing personality, she makes friends easily.
(她個性外向，很容易交到朋友。)
The outgoing principal gave a moving farewell speech.
(即將卸任的校長發表了感人的告別演說。)

outing(n.)出遊、短途旅行
(無詞性變化)
family outing 家庭出遊
school outing 校外教學
Our family went on an outing to Yangmingshan last Sunday.
(我們全家上週日到陽明山出遊。)
The class outing was canceled because of the typhoon.
(班級出遊因颱風而取消了。)

outlaw(n./v.)罪犯、亡命之徒、宣布⋯為非法
(無詞性變化)
outlaw smoking 禁止吸菸
a famous outlaw 知名的亡命之徒
Many countries have outlawed smoking in public places.
(許多國家已明令禁止在公共場所吸菸。)
The movie tells the story of a famous outlaw in the Wild West.
(這部電影講述蠻荒西部一位知名亡命之徒的故事。)

outlook(n.)觀點、看法、前景
(無詞性變化)
positive outlook 積極的人生觀
economic outlook 經濟前景
Despite her illness, she keeps a positive outlook on life.
(儘管生病，她仍保持積極的人生觀。)
Experts say the economic outlook for next year is uncertain.
(專家表示明年的經濟前景不明朗。)

outnumber(v.)數量上超過、比⋯多
(無詞性變化)
be outnumbered by 在數量上少於⋯
outnumber... by two to one 以二比一的比例超過⋯
In our class, girls outnumber boys by two to one.
(我們班女生人數是男生的兩倍。)
The soldiers were badly outnumbered but refused to give up.
(士兵們寡不敵眾，但拒絕投降。)

outrage(n./v.)憤慨、暴行、激怒
outrageous(adj.)駭人聽聞的
public outrage 公憤
express outrage 表達憤慨
The decision to cut down the old trees caused public outrage.
(砍伐老樹的決定引發了公憤。)
Many people were outraged by the cruel treatment of animals.
(許多人對虐待動物的行為感到憤慨。)

outrageous(adj.)駭人聽聞的、令人憤慨的、離譜的
outrage(n.)憤慨
outrageously(adv.)離譜地
outrageous price 離譜的價格
outrageous behavior 令人憤慨的行為
They charged an outrageous price for a simple meal.
(一頓簡單的餐點他們竟收取離譜的價格。)
His outrageous behavior at the party shocked everyone.
(他在派對上駭人的行為讓大家都很震驚。)

outright(adj./adv.)完全的、直率的、徹底地、當場
(無詞性變化)
win outright 完勝
outright lie 徹頭徹尾的謊言
What he told you was an outright lie.
(他告訴你的完全是謊言。)
She refused the offer outright without a second thought.
(她想都沒想就斷然拒絕了這個提議。)

outset(n.)開始、開端
(無詞性變化)
at the outset 一開始
from the outset 從一開始
From the outset, we knew the project would be difficult.
(我們從一開始就知道這個計畫會很困難。)
Make your goals clear at the outset of the semester.
(在學期一開始就把你的目標訂清楚。)

outskirts(n.)郊區、市郊
(無詞性變化)
on the outskirts of 在⋯的郊區
city outskirts 城市郊區
They moved to a quiet house on the outskirts of Taichung.
(他們搬到台中郊區一間安靜的房子。)
The new stadium was built on the outskirts of the city.
(新體育場蓋在城市的郊區。)

outward(adj.)外表的、向外的
outwardly(adv.)表面上
outward appearance 外表
outward journey 去程
Don't judge people by their outward appearance.
(不要以貌取人。)
Despite her outward calm, she was very nervous inside.
(儘管她外表平靜，內心卻非常緊張。)

outward(adv.)向外、往外
outwards(adv.)向外、往外(同 outward)
spread outward 向外擴散
open outwards 向外開
The door of the emergency exit opens outward.
(緊急出口的門是向外開的。)
The city has been expanding outwards for decades.
(這座城市數十年來不斷向外擴張。)

overdo(v.)做得過火、過度使用
overdone(adj.)煮過頭的、過度的
overdo it 做得過度、過度勞累
overdo the salt 鹽放太多
Exercise is good for you, but don't overdo it.
(運動對你有益，但不要過度。)
The chef overdid the salt, so the soup tasted terrible.
(廚師鹽放太多，所以湯很難喝。)

overflow(n./v.)溢出、氾濫、過剩
(無詞性變化)
overflow with 充滿⋯
overflow the banks 河水漫過堤岸
After days of heavy rain, the river overflowed its banks.
(連日大雨後，河水漫過了堤岸。)
Her heart was overflowing with joy on graduation day.
(畢業那天她的心中充滿了喜悅。)

overhear(v.)無意中聽到、偷聽到
(無詞性變化)
overhear a conversation 無意間聽到對話
be overheard 被人聽到
I happened to overhear my parents talking about a trip to Japan.
(我碰巧聽到爸媽在討論去日本旅行的事。)
Be careful what you say; you might be overheard.
(說話小心點，可能會被人聽到。)

overlap(n./v.)重疊、部分相同
(無詞性變化)
overlap with 與⋯重疊
a large overlap 大部分重疊
The two classes overlap, so I can only take one of them.
(這兩門課時間重疊，所以我只能選其中一門。)
There is some overlap between biology and chemistry.
(生物和化學之間有一些重疊的內容。)

overwork(n./v.)過勞、工作過度
overworked(adj.)工作過度的
die from overwork 過勞死
overworked and underpaid 工作過量且薪水過低
Overwork can lead to serious health problems.
(工作過度可能導致嚴重的健康問題。)
Nurses are often overworked during flu season.
(流感季節時護理師常常工作過量。)

oyster(n.)牡蠣、蚵仔
(無詞性變化)
oyster omelet 蚵仔煎
oyster sauce 蠔油
Oyster omelets are one of the most popular night market snacks.
(蚵仔煎是最受歡迎的夜市小吃之一。)
The world is your oyster, so go out and explore it.
(世界任你闖蕩，勇敢出去探索吧。)

ozone(n.)臭氧
(無詞性變化)
ozone layer 臭氧層
ozone hole 臭氧層破洞
The ozone layer protects the earth from harmful UV rays.
(臭氧層保護地球免受有害的紫外線傷害。)
Certain chemicals have caused a hole in the ozone layer.
(某些化學物質造成了臭氧層破洞。)
